title: Flowise MCP launcher -- T1562.001 npm_config_yes environment variable reproduces the --yes flag the patched blocklist only checks by name
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-69263 (GHSA-xc48-889x-5qmw),
affecting Flowise's MCP server launcher security check, an
incomplete fix for the earlier CVE-2025-8943.

The CVE-2025-8943 patch blocks the `-y`/`--yes` flags on `npx` to
stop auto-installation of arbitrary packages, and
`validateEnvironmentVariables()` in `MCP/core.ts` denies exactly four
hardcoded variable names by exact string match (`PATH`,
`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`). `npm` reads
its configuration directly from `npm_config_*` environment variables,
and `npm_config_yes=true` reproduces the exact `--yes` behavior the
flag filter exists to block -- it is not in the four-item blocklist,
so it passes through untouched. On a default Flowise deployment
(no authentication), an attacker-supplied MCP server config with
`env: {"npm_config_yes": "true"}` causes `npx` to auto-install and
execute an arbitrary named package as the Flowise process, even with
`CUSTOM_MCP_SECURITY_CHECK=true` enabled.

Detection logic flags an MCP server configuration whose `env` object
sets `npm_config_yes` (or the advisory's sibling bypass variables
`npm_config_prefix`, `npm_config_userconfig`, `NODE_PATH`,
`PYTHONPATH`, `PYTHONSTARTUP`) -- the exact denylist-by-name-only gap
this advisory's proof of concept exploits against a mitigation that
was believed closed.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (FlowiseAI, via
GHSA, citing the exact four-item blocklist source, the
`npm_config_yes` mechanism by name, a working PoC MCP config, and a
table of five additional untreated bypass variables across the other
permitted interpreters), fixed in Flowise 3.1.3 (verified via live GHSA lookup, 2026-09-04 -- the rule's original authoring predates the vendor's patch release; this note corrects a stale claim, not the detection logic itself).
